rule: Spring tides bloom salt-bloom in the tide-pools
texts: When a spring tide fills the tide-pools, salt-bloom blooms in the tide-pools.
Whenever a spring tide fills the tide-pools, salt-bloom grows in the tide-pools.
Salt-bloom is a pale crystalline crust.
Salt-bloom soon dissolves into the seawater.

fields.sentence: When a spring tide fills the tide-pools, salt-bloom blooms in the tide-pools.
parse: (: fill_bloom_rule (Implication (And (Member $x fill) (Agent $x $s) (Member $s spring_tide) (Patient $x sk_tide_pools_1)) (And (Member (sk_bloom $x) bloom) (Patient (sk_bloom $x) salt_bloom) (Location (sk_bloom $x) sk_tide_pools_1) (During (sk_bloom $x) $x))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

q2_gaps: a bare mass / non-count noun as the SUBJECT of a generic clause ("salt-bloom blooms in the tide-pools"): the instruction set licenses the bare kind symbol only as a non-specific OBJECT filler ("pays tax", "grows wheat") and routes bare-PLURAL generic subjects to a distributing rule over `(Member $x <kind>)`, leaving the mass-subject case — bare kind filler vs. witness vs. distributing rule — unaddressed
review.notes: `Patient` on "fills the tide-pools" (change of state) and `Patient` on the intransitive `bloom` subject (non-volitional natural process) both follow the stated role tests. The definite plural "the tide-pools" is correctly a top-level group witness, which is what licenses the `sk_*` constant appearing in the rule premise.

fields.sentence: Whenever a spring tide fills the tide-pools, salt-bloom grows in the tide-pools.
parse: (: tide_fill_bloom_grow (Implication (And (Member $x spring_tide) (Member $e1 fill) (Agent $e1 $x) (Patient $e1 sk_group_1)) (And (Member (sk_grow $e1) grow) (Patient (sk_grow $e1) salt_bloom) (Location (sk_grow $e1) sk_group_1) (During (sk_grow $e1) $e1))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

review.notes: The definite plural "the tide-pools" correctly becomes a top-level group witness, which is what licenses the sk_group_1 constant to appear in the rule premise; all three compounds emit head genus only. Patient on the intransitive change-of-state subject of grow and Location on the grow event (not LocatedIn, since an event anchors it) both match the stated tests.

fields.sentence: Salt-bloom is a pale crystalline crust.

q1_issues.issue: (Inheritance salt_bloom pale) carries (STV 1.0 0.9), but strength 1.0 is licensed only by an explicit all/every quantifier or by a definitional claim (which takes confidence 0.99); a bare generic at empirical confidence takes strength 0.9.
(Inheritance salt_bloom crystalline) has the same unlicensed 1.0/0.9 pairing - it should be either 0.9 0.9 as a bare empirical generic or 1.0 0.99 as definitional, not a mix of the two dials.

review.notes: Kind subject to Inheritance, the salt_bloom genus with the noun modifier suppressed, crystalline kept in its derived form, and the two descriptive adjectives split out instead of fused are all correct; only the two property atoms deviate on truth values.

issues.reason: Strength 1.0 on a generic is licensed only by an explicit all/every or by a definitional claim carrying confidence 0.99 ('dogs are mammals' 1.0 0.99), while a bare empirical generic takes 0.9 0.9 ('Trellises are wooden'), so (STV 1.0 0.9) on (Inheritance salt_bloom pale) matches no licensed dial setting.

(Inheritance salt_bloom crystalline) carries the same unlicensed pairing — the quantity rule puts a quantifierless generic at strength 0.9, and the confidence dial allows strength 1.0 only with definitional 0.99 confidence.

adjudication.defect_summary: For (Inheritance salt_bloom pale) the compliant form is (STV 0.9 0.9) as a bare empirical generic, or (STV 1.0 0.99) if the defining predicate is read as definitional; the same two licensed pairings are the compliant forms for (Inheritance salt_bloom crystalline).
adjudication.notes: The genus atoms, the crust predication at (1.0 0.99), the retained derived form 'crystalline', and the split of the two descriptive adjectives rather than fusion are all correct.

fields.sentence: Salt-bloom soon dissolves into the seawater.

q1_issues.issue: A bare generic verbal rule with no quantifier word takes strength 0.9 ('Birds fly' -> STV 0.9 0.9); strength 1.0 is reserved for an explicit all/every, so (STV 1.0 0.9) overstates the generalization.

q2_gaps: The temporal-proximity adverb 'soon' has no licensed slot - it falls in the sequence/ordering-adverb family the instruction set directs you to leave out and record - so the parse silently loses it.

A bare MASS noun as subject of a verbal generic ('Salt-bloom dissolves ...'): the instruction set licenses the distributing rule only for a bare plural or an explicit quantifier, and gives no reading for quantifying (Member $x salt_bloom) over instances of a mass kind.
review.notes: Both compound genus atoms (salt_bloom->bloom, seawater->water) are right, the noun modifiers are correctly left unexposed, and the definite 'the seawater' is properly a top-level constant outside the rule; Goal for 'into the seawater' is the licensed motion-result oblique.

issues.reason: Rule strength is set by the quantity — all/every 1.0, bare generic 0.9 ('Birds fly' at (STV 0.9 0.9)) — so (STV 1.0 0.9) on the quantifierless dissolve rule over-asserts the generalization.

gaps_confirmed: 'soon' — a temporal-proximity adverb with no licensed slot (the sequence/ordering-adverb family the instruction set directs be left out and recorded)

a bare MASS noun as subject of a verbal generic — the distributing rule is licensed for bare plurals or explicit quantifiers, and quantifying (Member $x salt_bloom) over instances of a mass kind is unaddressed
adjudication.defect_summary: The compliant form is the same distributing rule at (STV 0.9 0.9).
adjudication.notes: The two genus atoms, the top-level constant for the definite 'the seawater' (the causeway precedent for definites in rules), Patient on the change-of-state undergoer, and the Goal oblique for 'into' are all licensed.
